Assembly.district-info: This district encompasses the Door County peninsula as well as Kewaunee County and a slice of Brown County. It's a likely Republican district.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Joel Kitchens, R-Sturgeon Bay, faces a challenge from Democrat Renee Paplham. Kitchens, who chairs the Assembly Education Committee, was first elected to the Assembly in 2014. Prior to that, he spent 14 years on the Sturgeon Bay Board of Education. Paplham would be "a representative who rises above partisan politics and takes on issues that improve the lives of working families,” she claimed in a statement announcing her campaign. But given the Republican slant of the district, she faces an uphill battle in November.
Assembly.primary-results: Kitchens easily defeated a Republican challenger, while Paplham did not have a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The district includes portions of Brown, Manitowoc and Outagamie counties. It's a safe Republican district.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Shae Sortwell, R-Two Rivers, faces a challenge from Democrat Alicia Saunders, a veteran who served in the Navy for several years during the early 2000s. First elected in 2018, Sortwell serves as chair of the Assembly Committee on Regulatory Licensing Reform. Given the strong Republican leanings of the district, Saunders remains a longshot to unseat Sortwell.
Assembly.primary-results: Both Sortwell and Saunders advanced. Neither had an opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This district stretches from the Appleton area across Calumet County and into Manitowoc County. It's a safe Republican district.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell:
Rep. Ron Tusler, R-Harrison, will be a heavy favorite to win this seat in November after fellow Rep. Ty Bodden, R-Hilbert, who was also drawn into this district, opted not to challenge him in the Republican primary. Tusler was first elected to the Assembly in 2016. He chairs the Assembly Judiciary Committee.

He faces a challenge from Democrat Emily Voight. Voight is a Calumet County Board member who challenged Tusler in 2020. Tusler won that race by 19 percentage points. Given that it's a safe Republican district, Tusler is once again a heavy favorite.
Assembly.primary-results: Both Tusler and Voight advanced, setting up a rematch of the 2020 general election. Neither had a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This district covers the eastern region of Oconto County and extends slightly into Brown County, northwest of Green Bay. It's a safe Republican district.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. David Steffen, R-Howard, faces Democrat Jane Benson of Suamico. She is marking her second run for Assembly after losing to Elijah Behnke in 2022 in the 89th District. Steffen was first elected to the Assembly in 2014. Given the strong Republican tilt of the district, it will be an uphill battle for Benson.
Assembly.primary-results: Steffen will face Benson after both soundly defeated their opponents.

Assembly.district-info: The district contains a slice of Brown County that stretches into eastern Outagamie County. It is a likely Republican seat in November.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell:
Freshman Rep. Joy Goeben, R-Hobart, is running for reelection for the first time. Elected in 2022, she serves as the co-chair of the Assembly Committee on Children and Families. In the most recent legislative session, she helped sponsor a series of Republican child care bills, though none of them became law.

She faces a challenge from Democrat Greg Sampson of Little Chute. But with such a heavy Republican bend to the district, Goeben is expected to win a second term comfortably.
Assembly.primary-results: Both Goeben and Sampson advanced. Neither candidate had a primary challenger.

Assembly.district-info: The rural district covers all of Menominee County, most of Shawano County and parts of Oconto, Brown and Waupaca counties. It includes small cities such as Clintonville and Shawano. It's a safe Republican district.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Elijah Behnke, R-Oconto, was drawn into the 4th District, but decided to run in the neighboring 6th against Rep. Peter Schmidt, R-Bonduel, instead. Behnke stated multiple reasons for his move, including a feud with his local party in Oconto County. Democrat Shirley Hinze, of Shawano, is challenging him, but the district favors Republicans.
Assembly.primary-results: Behnke defeated Rep. Peter Schmidt, an incumbent who had a criminal conviction for choking a worker on his farm, by a double-digit margin and will face Hinze who didn't have a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The Milwaukee area district stretches from Greenfield in the south to West Allis in the north. It is a likely Democratic district.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell:
After a dozen years in the Assembly, Rep. Daniel Riemer, D-Milwaukee, opted not to run for reelection, creating an opening in a likely Democratic seat in the Milwaukee area.

Democrat Karen Kirsch, who ran unopposed in the primary, said her top policy priority is making improvements to Wisconsin's health care system. She has endorsements from Democratic heavyweights U.S. Rep. Gwen Moore and Milwaukee Mayor Cavalier Johnson. On the Republican side, Lee Whiting has filed to run. Whiting previously ran for the Milwaukee Common Council. Kirsch is a heavy favorite given the Democratic tilt of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: Both Kirsch and Whiting advanced. Neither had a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The Milwaukee district encompasses a large portion of the city's south side. It is a safe Democratic seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Sylvia Ortiz-Velez, D-Milwaukee, won a primary challenge in a safe Democratic district that encompasses a large portion of Milwaukee's south side. Ortiz-Velez was first elected in 2020. She has also served on the Milwaukee County Board of Supervisors. In January, she was a co-sponsor of a bipartisan bill that would have decriminalized possession of small amounts of marijuana. She doesn't have an opponent on Nov. 5.
Assembly.primary-results: Ortiz-Velez soundly defeated a primary challenger and does not face a general election opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The Milwaukee district encompasses a large portion of the city's south side. It is a safe Democratic seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell:
This safe Democratic seat is open. Rep. Marisabel Cabrera, who had represented the district since 2019, was elected in April to serve as a Milwaukee County Circuit Court judge, meaning she could not run for re-election in November.

Priscilla Prado, a small business owner campaigning on improving public safety and bolstering access to health care, won the Democratic primary. She faces Ryan Antczak, a former corrections officer, who is running on improving public safety and cutting taxes. Given the partisan skew of the district, Prado is an overwhelming favorite in November.
Assembly.primary-results: Prado soundly defeated Espana and will face Antczak who did not have a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This district encompasses parts of the north side of Milwaukee stretching up to Glendale. It is a safe Democratic seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Darrin Madison, D-Milwaukee, does not have a primary or general election challenge this year. Madison was first elected in 2022. He was one of two Democrats who revived the Legislature's socialist caucus in 2023.
Assembly.primary-results: Madison won an uncontested primary. He does not have a general election opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This district includes parts of Milwaukee and Havenwoods State Forest. It is a Democratic safe seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: This seat is currently held by Democrat Dora Drake, who is running for state Senate. Sequanna Taylor won the Democratic primary. Taylor is a Milwaukee County supervisor and served for one term on the Milwaukee Public Schools Board of Directors. She plans to boost youth education, mental health, affordable housing and economic development. In addition, she wants to work on improved re-entry services and criminal record expungements.
Assembly.primary-results: Taylor soundly won the Democratic primary and does not face an opponent in the general election.

Assembly.district-info: This district encompasses portions of Milwaukee County running along the border with Waukesha County. It is a safe Democratic seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell:
Rep. LaKeshia Myers, D-Milwaukee, opted to run for an open state Senate seat in November, leaving open a safe Democratic seat in the Milwaukee area.

Russell Goodwin, a reverend and former Milwaukee County Board of Supervisors member, won a four-way Democratic primary. He faces independent candidate Deanna Alexander. Alexander is a member of the Milwaukee County Board of Supervisors and a former Republican who is "proudly (running) as an independent, guided by the principle of prioritizing people over politics," according to a campaign launch statement.
Assembly.primary-results: Goodwin won a close four-way primary contest with about a third of the vote and does not have an opponent in the general election.

Assembly.district-info: This district covers Wauwatosa, Brookfield and Elm Grove. It leans Democratic.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Tom Michalski, R-Elm Grove, faces Rep. Robyn Vining, D-Wauwatosa, who currently represents the 14th district. Michalski wants to work on law enforcement reform by ensuring the judicial system is held accountable for enforcing the law. Vining is focused on public education funding, reproductive rights and mental health. The district leans Democratic and could be a pickup for Democrats trying to win an Assembly majority.
Assembly.primary-results: Michalski soundly defeated a primary challenger and will face Vining who was uncontested.

Assembly.district-info: This Democratic-leaning district includes a part of West Allis, stretching west to the border of Milwaukee and Waukesha counties.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Robyn Vining was moved into the 13th Assembly District by redistricting. Angelito Tenorio, a former member of the West Allis Common Council who ran for state treasurer in 2022, won a three-way Democratic primary and faces Republican Jim Engstrand, a small business owner who served in the military for more than 25 years, is also running. On social media, he has said he's working to "Make America Great Again." Engstrand has previously run for public office in Texas, according to Ballotpedia. Independent candidate Steven Shevey said he's running "to fight for the middle class in Madison."
Assembly.primary-results: Tenorio won a close three-way primary contest and will face Engstrand who did not have a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This suburban Milwaukee seat includes portions of Pewaukee, Waukesha and Brookfield. It is a safe Republican seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Adam Neylon, R-Pewaukee, faces a challenge from Democrat Sarah Harrison, a small business owner from Brookfield. First elected to the Assembly in a 2013 special election, Neylon co-chairs the Legislature's powerful Joint Committee for Review of Administrative Rules. Given the partisan skew of the district, Neylon is a strong favorite to secure another term.
Assembly.primary-results: Both Neylon and Harrison advanced. Neither had an opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This Milwaukee district encompasses portions of the city's north and west sides. It is a safe Democratic seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Kalan Haywood, D-Milwaukee, does not face a general election challenger in this safe Democratic seat in the heart of Milwaukee. Haywood, who serves as assistant minority leader, was first elected in 2018. At 25 years old, he is among the younger members of the Assembly.
Assembly.primary-results: Haywood advanced. He did not have a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This Milwaukee area district is rooted in the city's west side. It is a safe Democratic seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Supreme Moore Omokunde, D-Milwaukee, does not face a general election challenger. He was first elected to the Assembly in 2020. He is the son of U.S. Rep. Gwen Moore, a heavyweight in Wisconsin Democratic politics who has represented Milwaukee in the U.S. House since 2005.
Assembly.primary-results: Moore Omokunde advanced and does not have a general election opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This Milwaukee area district is rooted in the city's west side and extends to portions of Wauwatosa. It is a safe Democratic seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell:
Rep. Evan Goyke, D-Milwaukee, will not seek reelection to this seat after being elected Milwaukee city attorney in April.

Margaret Arney, a Wauwatosa Common Council member, won the Democratic primary after being endorsed by Goyke, U.S. Rep. Gwen Moore and a slate of other Milwaukee Democratic.

Arney faces Republican Kevin Anderson. Given the partisan slant of the district, he faces an uphill battle in November.
Assembly.primary-results: Arney soundly defeated her primary opponent and will face Anderson who didn't have a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This district covers downtown Milwaukee and its Lake Michigan waterfront. It is a safe Democratic seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Ryan Clancy, D-Milwaukee, an outspoken critic of the war in Gaza who supported a protest vote effort against President Biden in April’s presidential primary, won a tough Democratic primary. He does not face a general election opponent.
Assembly.primary-results: Clancy, an avowed socialist and Gaza war critic, won by 14 points over challenger Jarrod Anderson, who had strong backing from Milwaukee's Jewish community. Clancy does not face a general election opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The district stretches from the south side of Milwaukee along the lakefront to South Milwaukee, including communities like Cudahy and St. Francis. It is a likely Democratic seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Longtime Rep. Christine Sinicki faces a challenge from Republican Mike Moeller, a business executive from South Milwaukee. Sinicki was first elected in 1998 and has been a player in Milwaukee and Democratic politics for decades. Given the partisan skew of the district, she is a strong favorite to win another term.
Assembly.primary-results: Both Sinicki and Moeller advanced. Neither had a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This suburban Milwaukee seat encompasses portions of South Milwaukee and Oak Creek. This is a toss-up seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Jessie Rodriguez, R-Oak Creek, who was first elected to the Assembly in November 2013, could be at risk of losing her seat in this Democratic-leaning toss-up district. Rodriguez, who serves as a Republican member of the powerful Joint Finance Committee, faces a challenge from Democrat David Marstellar. Marstellar is a businessman and health care advocate.
Assembly.primary-results: Both Rodriguez and Marstellar advanced. Neither candidate had a contested primary.

Assembly.district-info: This suburban Milwaukee district encompasses Port Washington, Grafton, Cedarburg and parts of Mequon. It is a safe Republican seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Paul Melotik, R-Grafton, is seeking a full term after first being elected in a July 2023 special election. He faces Democrat Dana Glasstein, an educator and one of the plaintiffs in the lawsuit that resulted in Wisconsin's gerrymandered voting maps being thrown out by the state Supreme Court. Melotik serves as vice chair of the Assembly Committee on Government Accountability and Oversight. He previously spent six years serving on the Grafton town board. Given the partisan lean of the district, he is a strong favorite in November.
Assembly.primary-results: Both Melotik and Glasstein advanced. Neither had a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This suburban Milwaukee district encompasses Whitefish Bay, Brown Deer, Bayside and parts of Mequon. It is a likely Democratic seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Deb Andraca, D-Whitefish Bay, is seeking a third term in the Assembly. She faces Republican Laurie O'Brien Wolf. Given the district's makeup, Andraca is a heavy favorite to win.
Assembly.primary-results: Andraca and O'Brien Wolf both advanced. Neither candidate faced a primary challenger.

Assembly.district-info: This safe Republican seat encompasses Menomonee Falls and Germantown.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: State Sen. Dan Knodl, R-Germantown, was drawn into the same district as Sen. Duey Stroebel, R-Saukville, and decided to run for the Assembly to avoid a costly primary. He previously served in the Assembly from January 2009 to May 2023. He faces Democrat William Walter, executive director of liberal group Our Wisconsin Revolution. Given the district's Republican tilt, Knodl is expected to win the seat.
Assembly.primary-results: Knodl defeated Rep. Janel Brandtjen, the only Wisconsin legislative candidate to be endorsed by Donald Trump, with two-thirds of the vote and will face Walter who was uncontested.

Assembly.district-info: This likely Republican seat runs along Lake Michigan, including Two Rivers and Manitowoc and running south toward Sheboygan.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Paul Tittl, R-Manitowoc, faces Democrat Stephen Welch. Tittl is expected to win given the district is favorable to Republicans.
Assembly.primary-results: Tittl defeated a primary opponent by a double-digit margin and will face Welch who didn't have a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This toss-up district encompasses the city of Sheboygan and runs south along the lakefront toward Oostburg.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Freshman Rep. Amy Binsfeld, R-Sheboygan, is in for a tough re-election campaign against Democrat Joe Sheehan, a former Sheboygan Area School District superintendent and current executive director of the Sheboygan County Economic Development Corp. This new toss-up district reunites the Democratic-leaning city of Sheboygan, which was split in half under the state's previous, gerrymandered districts. Binsfeld served as chair of the Speaker's Task Force on Truancy. She was also the lead author on a constitutional amendment that would require a two-thirds supermajority of the Legislature to approve sales, corporate and income tax increases. This toss-up race is one to watch as Democrats look to flip the Republican Assembly majority.
Assembly.primary-results: Both Binsfeld and Sheehan advanced. Neither candidate had a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This safe Republican seat includes Plymouth, Elkhart Lake, Malone and Kiel. It touches the outskirts of Fond du Lac.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: With longtime Rep. Terry Katsma, R-Oostburg, retiring, this is an open safe Republican seat rooted in Sheboygan County. Lindee Brill, who has worked in nonprofits, wants to ensure election integrity and advocate for anti-abortion policies. Brill won a Republican primary and faces Democrat Kay Ladson.
Assembly.primary-results: Brill narrowly defeated Hilbelink and will face Ladson in the general election.

Assembly.district-info: This district includes St. Croix County along with parts of western Dunn County and northeast Pierce County. It is a safe Republican seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rob Kreibich, executive director of New Richmond’s Chamber of Commerce, who previously served as a state representative for 14 years, will face Democrat Danielle Johnson in the general election. Given the heavy Republican slant of the district, Kreibich is a heavy favorite to win.
Assembly.primary-results: Kreibich eked out a win over Penfield and will face Danielle Johnson in the general election.

Assembly.district-info: This likely Republican district runs along the Mississippi River, encompassing Trempealeau, Buffalo, Pepin and Pierce counties.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Treig Pronschinske, R-Mondovi, faces Democrat Terrance Schoonover, a retired emergency management coordinator. Given the Republican slant of the district, Pronschinske is a heavy favorite.
Assembly.primary-results: Pronschinske and Schoonover both advanced. Neither had a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This toss-up district encompasses River Falls, extending north to Hudson.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Shannon Zimmerman, River Falls, is seeking a fifth term in the Assembly. He served on the Speaker's Task Force on Artificial Intelligence and also serves on the Legislature's powerful Joint Finance Committee. He faces a challenge from Democrat Alison Page, a former nurse who eventually became CEO of Western Wisconsin Health. She's running to protect abortion access in Wisconsin and improve health care in rural parts of the state, according to her campaign website. The district is one to watch as Democrats try to win an Assembly majority.
Assembly.primary-results: Zimmerman and Page both advanced. Neither faced a primary challenger.

Assembly.district-info: This safe Republican seat encompasses Elkhorn, Walworth and Delavan.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Assembly Majority Leader Tyler August, R-Walworth, moved into this safe Republican seat to avoid a primary with Rep. Amanda Nedweski, R-Pleasant Prairie. That still resulted in an incumbent pairing with freshman Rep. Ellen Schutt, who decided not to run for reelection. August faces Democrat John Henderson, of Elkhorn, a retired real estate worker. August, the second-ranking Republican member of the Assembly and a close ally of Speaker Robin Vos, is a heavy favorite, given the partisan makeup of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: Both August and Henderson advanced from the Aug. 13 primary. Neither ran in a contested primary.

Assembly.district-info: This safe Republican district stretches from Lake Michigan along the Illinois border to Genoa City. It encompasses Twin Lakes, Paddock Lake and portions of Pleasant Prairie.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Amanda Nedweski, R-Pleasant Prairie, a freshman seeking a second term, also serves on the Kenosha County Board of Supervisors. During the most recent legislative session, she co-authored a 14-week abortion ban that did not include exceptions for rape or incest. She faces Democrat Michael Dhindsa. Nedweski is a heavy favorite to win a second term, given the strong Republican lean of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: Nedweski and Dhindsa both advanced from the Aug. 13 primary. Neither faced an opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This district encompasses Walworth County and southwest Racine. It is a Republican safe seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Assembly Speaker Robin Vos, the longest-serving Assembly speaker in state history, faces independent Kelly Clark and Democrat Alan Kupsik in the general election. Vos is a heavy favorite to win given the Republican tilt of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: Vos and Kupsik both advanced from the Aug. 13 primary. Vos' primary challenger dropped out of the race, but still received more than 30% of the vote. Clark will also appear on the ballot in November.

Assembly.district-info: This likely Republican district is rooted in Rhinelander, running north to the Wisconsin-upper peninsula border.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Rob Swearingen, R-Rhinelander, faces Democrat Dennis Nitzel. First elected in 2012, Swearingen chairs the Assembly Committee on State Affairs. He is a favorite to win given the partisan tilt of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: Swearingen and Nitzel both advanced from Aug. 13 primary. Neither candidate had a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This district includes all of Lincoln and Langlade counties and portions of Marathon, Shawano and Octono counties. It is a safe Republican seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell:
Republican incumbent Rep. Calvin Callahan faces Democratic challenger Lincoln County Supervisor Elizabeth McCrank in the Nov. 5 election. Callahan is favored to win given the partisan lean of the district.

Callahan has served as chair of the Consumer Protection Committee and vice chair of the Forestry, Parks and Outdoor Recreation Committee and the Insurance Committee. In the Legislature, he worked to reduce taxes and supported legislation that would have banned gender-affirming care for minors. 

McCrank is on the Board of Canvass and the Solid Waste Committee in Lincoln County and also served on the Lincoln County Land Services, Highway, Social Services and Emergency Planning Committees. She wants to enhance government transparency, protect reproductive healthcare and help local communities develop custom solutions.
Assembly.primary-results: Callahan soundly defeated primary challenger Todd Mayr and will face McCrank who did not have a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This district is rooted in Marinette and extends to encompass portions of Florence and Forest counties. It is a safe Republican seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Longtime Rep. Jeffrey Mursau, R-Crivitz, faces Democrat Ben Murray, a Navy veteran. Mursau chairs both the Assembly Committee on Forestry, Parks and Outdoor Recreation and the Legislature's Special Committee on State-Tribal Relations. Mursau was one of the lead authors during the most recent legislative session that would have directed how $125 million is used to address PFAS contamination throughout the state. Murray is running to "limit out-of-touch career politicians and draw focus back to our working class," according to his campaign website. He is a heavy underdog, given the makeup of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: Mursau and Murray both advanced. Neither had a primary challenger.

Assembly.district-info: This safe Republican seat encompasses Beaver Dam, Fox Lake, Waupun and Mayville.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Mark Born, R-Beaver Dam, faces Democrat LaToya Bates, of Mayville. Born, who was first elected in 2012, co-chairs the Legislature's powerful budget writing committee, making him one of the most influential Republicans working at the Capitol. Born is a heavy favorite given the partisan makeup of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: Born soundly defeated Rydzewski and will face Bates who was uncontested.

Assembly.district-info: This safe Republican seat stretches from Jefferson north to Johnson Creek and Watertown, extending all the way to Juneau.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Incumbent Rep. William Penterman, R-Columbus, faces Democrat Izzy Hassey Nevarez, of Juneau. Penterman, who was first elected in a July 2021 special election, chairs the Assembly Committee on Labor and Integrated Employment. He is a heavy favorite given the partisan lean of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: Penterman and Nevarez both advanced. Neither faced a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This district includes Green Lake, Marquette, and Fond du Lac County communities. It is a safe Republican seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell:
Republican incumbent Rep. Alex Dallman, R-Green Lake, faces Democrat Chris Gordon, a career teacher and school administrator. Dallman is favored to win given the partisan slant of the district.

Dallman currently represents the 41st Assembly District, but with the new maps will run for the 39th. He wants to continue reducing taxes, increasing a skilled workforce and strengthening agricultural sectors in his district. 

Gordon listed on her website she wants to boost local economies, clean water and educational funding. She also wants to work toward universal healthcare and more affordable housing.
Assembly.primary-results: Dallman and Gordon both advanced. Neither faced a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The 40th district covers small cities like Baraboo and Portage and also includes several rural communities west of Prairie du Sac. It is a likely Democratic district.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Karen DeSanto, of Baraboo, faces Republican Gerald Helmer of Prairie du Sac, following the retirement of Rep. Dave Considine, D-Baraboo. DeSanto, the former CEO of the Boys & Girls Clubs of West Central Wisconsin, is favored due to the partisan slant of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: DeSanto defeated two opponents in the Democratic primary with about two-thirds of the Aug. 13 primary vote and will face Helmer who was uncontested.

Assembly.district-info: This district includes Richland Center, Reedsburg and the Wisconsin Dells. It is a Republican-leaning district.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Three-term Rep. Tony Kurtz, R-Wonewoc, faces Democrat Julia Henley, a developer from Blue River. She is campaigning on environmental sustainability, boosting public education funding and expanding health care access and abortion rights. Kurtz, who was first elected in 2018, serves on the Legislature's powerful budget writing committee. He was influential during the last legislative session in passing a bill that boosted state financial aid to local governments, including allowing the city of Milwaukee and Milwaukee County to assess additional sales taxes to raise revenue. The district leans Republican, but the race is one to watch to gauge if a Democratic wave is materializing.
Assembly.primary-results: Kurtz and Henley both advanced. Neither faced a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: Assembly district 42 includes DeForest, Windsor and parts of Northeast Madison. It is a safe Democratic seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Democrat Maureen McCarville has served on the Dane County Board for 12 years representing DeForest and Windsor. She faces Republican Rebecca Witherspoon who is a village trustee in DeForest. McCarville's goals include reducing recidivism and addressing mental health issues. Witherspoon is focused on sustainability and affordable housing developments. McCarville is favored to win due to the partisan lean of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: McCarville and Witherspoon both advanced. Neither faced a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This southern Wisconsin district comprises parts of Rock County, Walworth County and Jefferson County. It includes the cities of Whitewater, Edgerton and Milton, part of the city of Janesville and the University of Wisconsin–Whitewater campus. It is a likely Democratic seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Scott Johnson of Jefferson was originally drawn into the heavily Republican 97th District with Rep. Cindi Duchow, R-Town of Delafield, but decided to move to the 43rd. Johnson is a farmer and former school bus driver who was first elected in 2022 to the 33rd District and says he ran for office after seeing how "Madison puts politics ahead of supporting farming and family values." He faces Democrat Brienne Brown of Whitewater, who has received a long list of endorsements and was elected to the Whitewater Common Council several times. She supports abortion rights, fair pay for teachers and improved access to broadband. Brown is favored to win due to the partisan makeup of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: Johnson soundly won a Republican primary and will face Brown who was uncontested.

Assembly.district-info: This southern Wisconsin district comprises parts of Rock County, including the city of Janesville and the village of Footville. It includes the University of Wisconsin–Whitewater at Rock County campus and the main campus of Blackhawk Technical College. This is a safe Democratic seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Incumbent Rep. Sue Conley, D-Janesville, will not seek reelection and has backed Ann Roe, of Janesville, to succeed her. Roe, a small business owner and former college educator, has received a long list of endorsements. She faces Bruce Danielson, a Janesville police officer. Roe is favored to win in the heavily Democratic district.
Assembly.primary-results: Roe won the Democratic primary and will face Danielson who was uncontested.

Assembly.district-info: This likely Democratic seat stretches in an "L" shape from Evansville to Beloit.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Clinton Anderson, D-Beloit, faces no primary or general election in this likely Democratic seat, which encompasses the city of Beloit. He was one of the lead author's in the most recent legislative session on a law that requires a disclosure when campaign communications feature content generated by artificial intelligence.
Assembly.primary-results: Anderson advanced. He did not face a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This likely Democratic seat in the Madison area includes portions of Cottage Grove, stretching east to Lake Mills and south to Fort Atkinson.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Melissa Ratcliff, D-Cottage Grove, who currently represents this seat, opted not to seek a second term and is instead running for an open state Senate seat. Joan Fitzgerald of Fort Atkinson, a retired public school teacher and former member of the Jefferson County Board of Supervisors, is running against Republican Waterloo Mayor Jenifer Quimby, who was elected to her current role in 2019, the first woman to hold the post. Fitzgerald is favored due to the partisan lean of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: Fitzgerald and Quimby both advanced. Neither faced a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The district includes Fitchburg, Stoughton and part of McFarland in Dane County. It is a safe Democratic seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Telecommunications professional Randy Udell, a former Fitchburg alderman, is running as a policymaker who can use his 30 years of engineering experience with AT&T to expand broadband. He won the Democratic primary and doesn't face a general election opponent.
Assembly.primary-results: Udell won a close Democratic primary and does not face an opponent in the general election.

Assembly.district-info: This safe Democratic seat is anchored in Sun Prairie and stretches northeast toward Columbus.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Andrew Hysell, an attorney endorsed by several Madison area state lawmakers, faces Republican Lisa Rubrich. Hysell is favored to win in the heavily Democratic district.
Assembly.primary-results: Hysell won the five-way primary with about a third of the vote and will face Rubrich who did not have a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This toss-up district in western Wisconsin runs along the Mississippi River, encompassing portions of Grant and Crawford counties.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Longtime Rep. Travis Tranel, R-Cuba City, faces a challenge from Democrat Scott Walker (not the former governor). Walker is a doctor who runs a medical clinic in the district for the "underserved and uninsured." Boosting public school funding is among his top campaign priorities. Tranel, who was first elected to the Assembly in 2010, chairs the Assembly Committee on Agriculture. Tranel is a dairy farmer who grew up in the area. The race is one to watch for signs of a Democratic wave.
Assembly.primary-results: Tranel and Walker both advanced. Neither faced a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The district encompasses Green County and is located in southern Wisconsin including the cities of New Glarus and Monroe. It is a likely Democratic district.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Jenna Jacobson, D-Oregon, faces Republican challenger Rich Johnson. Jacobson took office in 2023 representing the 43rd District. She has prioritized working on public education and co-authoring bills to fund schools, support rural communities, incentivize new farmers and fund childcare. She also previously served on the Oregon Village Board. Johnson has not posted public information on policies he supports. Jacobson is favored to win due to the Democratic tilt of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: Jacobson and Johnson both advanced. Neither faced a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This likely Democratic seat is rooted in Dodgeville and stretches south to the Wisconsin-Illinois border.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Longtime Rep. Todd Novak, R-Dodgeville, will face a tough reelection test in this redrawn district. Novak, who was first elected to the Assembly in 2014, also serves as mayor of Dodgeville, a role he has held for more than a decade. Democrat Elizabeth Grabe, a real estate agent and farm manager, is challenging him. The district leans heavily Democratic, but Novak has survived Democratic challenges in the past.
Assembly.primary-results: Novak and Grabe both advanced. Neither faced a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This district includes parts of Appleton, Fox Crossing and Menasha. It leans Democratic.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Lee Snodgrass, D-Appleton, faces Republican Chad Cooke, who ran for Outagamie County Board in 2021, is a veteran and former Corrections officer who advertises himself as change maker who wants to educate citizens on local government decisions and how committees work. He said he stands for a transparent but limited government and is a supporter of law enforcement, first responders and correction officers. Snodgrass, who took office in 2021, has fought against conversion therapy in the state, supports mental health and sports participation for Wisconsin’s LGBTQ+ youth. The district's partisan makeup favors Snodgrass.
Assembly.primary-results: Snodgrass and Cooke both advanced. Neither faced a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The 53rd District lies in the middle of the Fox Valley, encompassing Neenah and Menasha. It is a toss-up district.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: First-time candidate Duane Shukoski, a lifelong resident of Neenah, is running as a Democrat. Shukoski is running on a platform emphasizing climate reform, increasing education funding and supporting abortion access. Republican Dean Kaufert is hoping to return to politics after serving as mayor of Neenah for eight years. Kaufert was previously a member of the Assembly, representing the 55th District from 1991 to 2015. The race is one to watch to see if Democrats can win an Assembly majority.
Assembly.primary-results: Shukoski and Kaufert both advanced. Neither faced a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The 54th District includes Oshkosh. The seat leans Democratic.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell:
Rep. Lori Palmeri, D-Oshkosh, is seeking re-election against Republican veteran Tim Paterson. Palmeri is favored to win given the political composition of the district.

Palmeri, who took office in 2023, was the first female mayor of Oshkosh. She has worked on University of Wisconsin-Oshkosh’s budget crisis, protecting diversity initiatives and low enrollment. She also champions women’s reproductive rights and Medicaid expansion. She serves on the Committee on Environment and also Forestry, Parks and Outdoor Recreation, Mental Health and Substance Abuse Prevention. 

Paterson spent 33 years in the Army National Guard and Army Reserves. He was deployed twice overseas, served as a Blackhawk Pilot and retired as a lieutenant colonel. If elected, he wants to address inflation, the tax burden on the middle class and reduce crime in the area that he attributes to weak policies at the southern border. In addition, he supports educational transparency and providing students with a quality education.
Assembly.primary-results: Palmeri and Paterson both advanced. Neither faced a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This district covers most of Winnebago County and part of Outagamie County. It includes the city of Omro, the village of Winneconne, a portion of Fox Crossing and the southern quarter of Oshkosh. This is a likely Republican district.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Nate Gustafson, R-Fox Crossing, faces Democrat Kyle Kehoe, of Oshkosh. Gustafson, who was moved into the district and defeated incumbent Rep. Michael Schraa, was elected in 2022 and has advocated for younger Republican candidates like himself to step up. Gustafson also has a long list of endorsements, including former GOP presidential candidate Vivek Ramaswamy. He serves on the committees on Judiciary, State Affairs, Labor and Integrated Employment, Ways and Means, and Regulatory Licensing Reform, where he is the vice chair. He was also appointed chair to the Speaker’s Task Force on Artificial Intelligence. Gustafson is favored to win due to the partisan composition of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: Gustafson defeated Schraa by a double-digit margin in a primary pitting two GOP incumbents against each other. He will face Kehoe who didn't have a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This safe Republican district stretches northwest from the outskirts of Appleton to encompass New London and Bear Creek.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Longtime Rep. David Murphy, R-Greenville, faces Democrat Emily Tseffos, of Appleton. First elected in 2012, Murphy currently chairs the Assembly Committee on Colleges and Universities, giving him influence in GOP lawmakers' ongoing feud with the UW System over diversity, equity and inclusion efforts. Tseffos is campaigning on boosting funding for public schools and bolstering abortion rights in Wisconsin. She is an underdog, given the partisan makeup of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: Murphy and Tseffos both advanced. Neither faced a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This safe Republican seat includes Waupaca, stretching south to Wautoma.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Kevin Petersen, R-Waupaca, faces Democrat Ruth Caves, of Wild Rose, and independent Dylan Testin. Petersen was first elected to the Assembly in 2006, oversees Assembly floor sessions in his role as speaker pro tempore and is vice chair of the Legislature's powerful Joint Committee for Review of Administrative Rules. Petersen is favored to win because of the district's partisan makeup.
Assembly.primary-results: Petersen soundly defeated Wilson and faces Caves, who didn't have a primary opponent, and Testin in the general election.

Assembly.district-info: Encompassing Slinger and West Bend, this is a safe Republican seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Incumbent Rep. Rick Gundrum, R-Slinger, faces Democrat Deb Anderson, a retiree who has lived in West Bend for decades. First elected in 2018, Gundrum serves as chair of the Assembly Committee on Jobs, Economy and Small Business Development. Given the partisan skew of the district, he is a strong favorite.
Assembly.primary-results: Gundrum and Anderson both advanced. Neither faced a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The 59th Assembly District is largely rural, falling south of Fond du Lac and Sheboygan and north of the Milwaukee metropolitan area. The district includes parts of Ozaukee, Washington, Sheboygan, Fond du Lac and Dodge counties. It is a safe Republican seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Incumbent Rep. Robert Brooks, R-Saukville, faces Democrat Jack Holzman, a retired teacher from Belgium, Wisconsin. First elected in 2014, Brooks chairs the Assembly Committee on Housing and Real Estate. Prior to be elected to the Assembly, he served on the Ozaukee County Board for 14 years. Holzman is running because his "core values are being challenged by the far right and the Republican Party," according to his campaign site. Brooks is a heavy favorite to win another term because of the partisan makeup of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: Brooks and Holzman both advanced. Neither faced a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The 60th Assembly District encompasses Fond du Lac, stretching north across Dexter and Van Dyne toward the Winnebago County border. It is a likely Republican district.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: In a rematch from 2022, first-term Rep. Jerry O'Connor, R-Fond du Lac, faces Democrat Joe Lavrenz of Fond du Lac. During the most recent legislative session, O'Connor chaired the Speaker's Task Force on Human Trafficking. Lavrenz has spent his career working for telecommunications companies and in IT. O'Connor is favored to win because of the partisan composition of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: O'Connor and Lavrenz both advanced. Neither faced a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The 61st Assembly District covers the southwestern Milwaukee villages of Greendale and Hales Corners and parts of Greenfield. It is a toss-up district.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: This district features a rematch from 2022. Freshman Rep. Bob Donovan, R-Greenfield, will once again face off against Democrat LuAnn Bird, whom he defeated by just a few hundred voters. Donovan served on the Milwaukee Common Council for 20 years and ran for mayor in April 2022. In the Legislature, he serves as vice chair of the Assembly Committee on Local Government. He's running for re-election because the district "needs a tested fighter for public safety and the interests of the common man, woman, and child, to bridge the gap between Madison and local governments," according to his campaign website. Bird, who is a former executive director and lobbyist for the League of Women Voters of Wisconsin, is running because "extreme MAGA politicians are taking away women's rights to reproductive health care" and "blocking common-sense gun safety laws that would save lives and make our communities safer," according to her campaign website. The district is one to watch to see if Republicans can hold on to their Assembly majority.
Assembly.primary-results: Donovan won his Republican primary and will face Bird who didn't have an opponent. It is a rematch of a 2022 contest.

Assembly.district-info: The 62nd Assembly District covers the northern part of Racine, including the villages of North Bay and Wind Point. It is a safe Democratic seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Angelina Cruz, president of Racine Educators United, the teachers union in Racine, is running unopposed as a Democrat. She is running to boost funding for public schools and celebrated a recent ruling that found portions of Act 10 are unconstitutional.
Assembly.primary-results: Cruz advanced. She did not face a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The 63rd Assembly District lies in between Racine and South Milwaukee, including parts of the village of Caledonia to the southeast and encompassing Franklin toward the northwest. It is a likely Republican seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Robert Wittke, R-Racine, is the only candidate vying for this likely Republican seat. He is moving into this district after being drawn into the safe Democratic 62nd District. First elected in 2018, Wittke serves as co-chair of the Joint Legislative Audit Committee.
Assembly.primary-results: Wittke advanced. He did not face an opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The 64th Assembly District includes part of Kenosha County, the villages of Somers and the northern half of the city of Kenosha. The seat is likely Democratic.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: In a 2022 rematch, Rep. Tip McGuire, D-Kenosha, faces a rematch from Republican Ed Hibsch. Hibsch, who worked with data analytics then opened a luxury transportation business in Kenosha, is running to help citizens with taxes and managing a business. He is a board member for the Republican Party of Kenosha County. McGuire, who took office in 2019, has supported tax relief for small businesses and working families. He serves on the Joint Finance, Criminal Justice and Public Safety and Sporting Heritage committees. McGuire is favored due to the partisan makeup of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: McGuire and Hibsch both advanced. Neither faced a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The 65th Assembly District covers downtown Kenosha and southern parts of Kenosha County, as well as the northern half of the village of Pleasant Prairie. It is a likely Democratic district.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Tod Ohnstad, D-Kenosha, announced he won't seek reelection after serving for a dozen years. Ben DeSmidt of Kenosha, will face former Kenosha police officer Brian Gonzales, a Republican, who is running to improve public safety. DeSmidt, who has been endorsed by Ohnstad, is a former educator and small business owner. He is focused on health care affordability, protecting abortion rights and expanding affordable opportunities for education. DeSmidt is favored to win due to the partisan composition of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: DeSmidt soundly won the Democratic primary and will face Gonzales who was uncontested.

Assembly.district-info: The 66th Assembly District includes southern parts of Racine and borders with Interstate 94 on the west, encompassing Elmwood Park and Sturtevant. It is a likely Democratic seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Assembly Minority Leader Greta Neubauer, D-Racine, faces Republican David DeGroot, who currently serves as Mount Pleasant village president, is campaigning on cutting taxes, empowering parents in schools and supporting small businesses, according to his campaign website. DeGroot, who was re-elected to his current role 18 months ago, faced a bitter challenge in April 2023 over his role in bringing Foxconn to Mount Pleasant. He and allied incumbents emerged victorious in their respective races, but the campaign became a partisan political slugfest. First elected to the Assembly in a January 2018 special election, Neubauer has led the Assembly Democratic caucus for the past two and a half years. Neubauer began her career working as a climate activist. Since taking office, she has continued working on those issues, and is a leading voice among Democrats on abortion rights and preserving democracy. Neubauer is favored due to the partisan composition of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: Neubauer and DeGroot both advanced. Neither faced a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The 67th Assembly District covers a largely rural area in parts of Menomonie, Dunn and Chippewa counties along with the entirety of Barron County and is a likely Republican seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Incumbent Rep. David Armstrong, R-Rice Lake, faces Democrat Jeffrey Foster of Colfax. Armstrong has been a member of the Assembly since 2021. In 2020, it was reported that Armstrong had a history of promoting QAnon conspiracy theories on social media and shared a racist video featuring former Ku Klux Klan Grand Wizard David Duke. Armstrong is favored to win due to the partisan composition of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: Armstrong soundly won the Democratic primary and will face Foster who was uncontested.

Assembly.district-info: The 68th Assembly District is a largely rural district covering Price and Rusk counties, along with parts of Chippewa and Taylor counties. It is a safe Republican district.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Rob Summerfield, R-Bloomer, chair of the Majority Caucus, faces Democrat Richard Pulcher, of Lublin, who has worked as a union steward for nearly two decades and was a volunteer firefighter for 20 years. Summerfield has held office since 2017. He has helped operate several small businesses around the Chippewa Valley. Summerfield is favored to win due to the partisan composition of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: Summerfield defeated Taylor by a comfortable margin and will face Pulcher who was uncontested.

Assembly.district-info: Assembly District 69 is a largely rural area that lies east of Eau Claire and west of Wausau. The district encompasses the entirety of Clark County alongside parts of Chippewa, Taylor and Marathon counties. It is a safe Republican seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Freshman Rep. Karen Hurd, R-Fall Creek, faces Democrat Roger Halls, a military veteran who sat on the Stanley City Council for six years. He's running to boost school funding and address the cost of living crisis facing many Wisconsin residents. Hurd is moving into the district after being drawn into the Democratic-leaning 91st Assembly District. She chaired the Speaker's Task Force on Childhood Obesity during the most recent legislative session. She's campaigning for reelection on cutting taxes, supporting law enforcement and empowering parents in the educational setting. Hurd is favored to win due to the partisan composition of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: Hurd won the Republican primary by a double-digit margin and faces Halls who didn't have a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The 70th Assembly District is a rural district that covers the entirety of Jackson County and stretches southward into parts of Monroe and Juneau counties. It is a likely Republican seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Nancy VanderMeer, R-Tomah, faces Democrat Remy Gomez, also from Tomah. First elected in 2014, VanderMeer chairs the Assembly Transportation Committee and serves as Republican Caucus Secretary. Gomez serves on the Monroe County Board of Supervisors. He's running because he believes the district "needs a representative in Madison who will work for everyone." VanderMeer is favored to win due to the partisan composition of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: Both VanderMeer and Gomez advanced without an opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The 71st Assembly District encompasses Stevens Point and stretches southward, including portions of Portage and Adams counties. It is bordered by Wood County to the west and Waupaca County to the east. The district leans Democratic.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Long-time Rep. Katrina Shankland opted to run for Congress, though lost in the Democratic primary. Vinnie Miresse, a Portage County Board member and owner of a residential remodeling business, faces Bob Pahmeier, a former Federal Bureau of Prisons correctional officer. Miresse is campaigning on increasing bipartisan cooperation in the Capitol, investing in public schools and protecting abortion rights. Pahmeier is campaigning on building affordable housing, bolstering small businesses and family farms and promoting parental involvement in education. Miresse is favored to win in the Democratic-leaning district.
Assembly.primary-results: Both Miresse and Pahmeier advanced without an opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The 72nd Assembly District encompasses part of Juneau County, the southern half of Wood County and the northern half of Adams County. It is a likely Republican seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell:
Incumbent Rep. Scott Krug, R-Nekoosa, is seeking re-election against Democrat Suzanne Campbell. Krug is favored due to the partisan makeup of the district.

Krug took office in 2011 and is the chair on the Committee on Campaigns and Election. He also sits on the Committee on Colleges and Universities, Committee on Housing and Real Estate and Committee on Local Government. Recently, he has sponsored legislation to address absentee ballot certificates, workforce home loan programs and tax reductions.

Campbell worked in the credit union industry for 25 years and leads the creative team for Exclamation Services in Marshfield. According to her social media posts, she supports LGBTQ+ equality, Juneteenth and women in politics including Democratic Secretary of State Sarah Godlewski.
Assembly.primary-results: Both Krug and Campbell advanced without an opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The 73rd Assembly District is a rural district that borders Minnesota to the west and Lake Superior to the north. It includes parts of Douglas, Bayfield and Ashland counties and encompasses the Bad River and Red Cliff Ojibwe Reservations. It is a safe Democratic seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Incumbent Angie Sapik, R-Lake Nebagamon, announced she would not seek reelection. Republican Frank Kostka of Ashland faces Democrat Angela Stroud. Kostka served as Department Commander for the Wisconsin American Legion in 2019 and is now a member of the Wisconsin American Legion Board of Directors. Stroud, who lives in the town of Gingles, is a longtime educator. She currently works as an associate professor of sociology and social justice at Northland College. After redistricting the former Republican seat is now a safe Democratic seat.
Assembly.primary-results: Stroud soundly won the Democratic primary and faces Kostka who did not have a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The 74th Assembly District covers a rural part of northern Wisconsin, bordering Minnesota to its west and Michigan's Upper Peninsula to its east. The district includes the entireties of Sawyer, Iron and Washburn counties along with parts of Burnett, Douglas, Bayfield and Ashland Counties, and is a likely Republican seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: First-term Rep. Chanz Green, R-Grand View, is seeking re-election against Democrat Jeanne Bruce. Green has focused on hunting rights, workforce development and infrastructure spending. Bruce, who has served on the Washburn County Board of Commissioners, retired after a 30-year career in program and fund development in business, government and the nonprofit sector. She supports reproductive rights and rural health care, restructuring the hospital system and protecting natural resources. Green is favored to win due to the partisan composition of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: Green won the Democratic primary and faces Bruce who did not have a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The 75th Assembly District encompasses Polk County and the southern portion of Burnett County in a largely rural area, and it shares its western border with Minnesota. It is a safe Republican seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Gae Magnafici, R-Dresser, announced in March that she would be retiring. Duke Tucker of Grantsburg, a first-time Assembly candidate endorsed by Magnafici, faces Democrat Jane Kleiss, of St. Croix Falls. Tucker has proposed using the National Guard to secure the state border and enforcing criminalization of undocumented immigrants. Kleiss, who is a parent and has worked as a chef, supports increasing access to childcare, healthcare and housing, protecting natural resources and abortion rights. Tucker is favored to win due to the partisan composition of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: Tucker defeated two opponents with about half the vote and faces Kleiss who did not have a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This district includes the isthmus and east and north sides of Madison. It is a safe Democratic seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Francesca Hong, D-Madison, is running unopposed for reelection. In the Legislature, Hong has worked on protecting reproductive healthcare, the environment, minority-owned businesses and paid leave bills. She has also worked to fund UW System.
Assembly.primary-results: Hong won an uncontested primary and faces no general election challenger.

Assembly.district-info: Wisconsin's 77th Assembly District encompasses the University of Wisconsin-Madison campus, Shorewood Hills and Madison neighborhoods around Lake Wingra. It is a safe Democratic seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Renuka Mayadev works as an advisor for maternal and child health at UW’s School of Medicine and Public Health and is campaigning on education, gun violence, climate change and reproductive health care. She does not have an opponent in the general election.
Assembly.primary-results: Mayadev defeated two opponents with nearly half the vote and does not face an opponent in the general election.

Assembly.district-info: The 78th district includes south Madison, Monona, McFarland, Fitchburg and Blooming Grove. It is a safe Democratic seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Shelia Stubbs, D-Madison, Dane County’s first Black representative in the Legislature, is focused on criminal justice and missing and murdered African American women and girls. Stubbs has served in the Legislature since 2019. She does not have a general election opponent.
Assembly.primary-results: Stubbs defeated Pearson with almost two-thirds of the vote and does not face an opponent in the general election.

Assembly.district-info: This district covers the west side of Madison and is a safe Democratic seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Lisa Subeck, D-Madison, is unopposed running for Wisconsin’s 79th Assembly district. She currently represents the 78th District but was moved due to redistricting. Subeck has served in the Legislature since 2015, and is focused on accessible health care, reproductive rights, education funding and protecting natural resources.
Assembly.primary-results: Subeck won an uncontested primary and faces no general election challenger.

Assembly.district-info: This district includes Verona, Cross Plains, Middleton and parts of west and southwest Madison. It is a safe Democratic seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Incumbent Rep. Mike Bare, D-Verona, faces Republican Robert Relph in the general November election. Bare’s top priority is investing in K-12 education, housing and transit expansion and boosting initiatives for low-income homeowners and renters. Bare is favored to win because the district strongly favors Democrats.
Assembly.primary-results: Bare soundly won the Democratic primary and will face Relph who was uncontested.

Assembly.district-info: The district lies on the northwest border of Lake Mendota, covering the Madison suburbs of Middleton and Waunakee. It is a safe Democratic seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Incumbent Rep. Alex Joers, D-Middleton, faces no general election challenger in this safe Democratic seat. Originally, drawn into the 80th District alongside Rep. Mike Bare, Joers opted to move into the open seat to avoid an incumbent-vs-incumbent primary.
Assembly.primary-results: Joers won an uncontested primary and faces no general election challenger.

Assembly.district-info: The 82nd Assembly District covers much of the western and central portions of Waukesha. It is a likely Republican seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Incumbent Rep. Scott Allen, R-Waukesha, has represented the 97th Assembly District for nearly a decade. Now, after being redistricted into the 82nd Assembly District, he is running for reelection on a conservative platform supporting school voucher expansion and tax cuts while opposing abortion. During his tenure, Allen has proposed anti-trans legislation, introduced plans to prosecute school teachers and librarians for "obscene" books and has supported right-wing calls to impeach state elections administrator Meagan Wolfe. He faces Kevin Reilly of Waukesha, a psychiatric technician and the brother of Waukesha Mayor Shawn Reilly. Reilly supports abortion rights, statewide marijuana legalization and Medicaid expansion. Allen is favored due to the district's partisan makeup.
Assembly.primary-results: Reilly won the Democratic primary by a double-digit margin and will face Allen who didn't have a primary opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The 83rd Assembly District includes the southeastern portion of Waukesha, stretching eastward to also encompass New Berlin and parts of Muskego. It is a safe Republican seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Incumbent Rep. Dave Maxey, R-Berlin, faces Democrat Jill Schindler in the Nov. 5 election. Schindler does not have public information out about her campaign. Maxey has served in the Legislature since 2022 and is the vice chair of the Committee on Campaign and Elections, and participates in four other committees. He promotes himself as anti-abortion, an education reformer and an advocate for low property taxes. Maxey is favored to win in the heavily Republican district.
Assembly.primary-results: Both Maxey and Schindler advanced without an opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This district saddles the border between Waukesha and Racine counties, including Muskego, Mukwonago and Waterford. It is a safe Republican seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Chuck Wichgers, R-Muskego, faces a challenge from Democrat Zachary Roper in the Nov. 5 election. Roper does not have public information out about his campaign. Wichgers has served in the Assembly since 2016, serving on four committees. Wichgers is one of 15 Wisconsin Republican legislators who called on Vice President Mike Pence to overturn the 2020 election results. He supports the police system, anti-abortion principles, religious freedom, reducing drug usage and protecting gun rights. Wichgers is expected to win the seat due to its partisan composition.
Assembly.primary-results: Both Wichgers and Roper advanced without an opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The 85th Assembly District covers Wausau, extending to also include Weston to the east. The district is a toss-up between Democrats and Republicans.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell:
Incumbent Rep. Patrick Snyder, R-Schofield, faces a challenge from Democrat Yee Leng Xiong in the Nov. 5 election. The district is one to watch as Republicans try to defend their Assembly majority.

Xiong served on the DC Everest School Board and in 2016 secured a position on the Marathon County Board of Supervisors where he advocted for mental health services in schools, expanding a 911 dispatch line and enhacing public safety providers. He wants to fund domestic violence and sexual assault service providers and focus on the economy, enviroment and health care.

Snyder, who was elected to the Assembly since 2017, has spent time on the Schofield City Council. He has worked to improve broadband expansion, cut taxes, advocate for veterans and police, and alleviate the workforce crisis.
Assembly.primary-results: Both Snyder and Xiong advanced without an opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The central Wisconsin district covers half of Wood County, parts of Marathon County, and includes cities like Marshfield and Pittsville, as well as villages like Edgar, Spencer and Stratford. It's a safe Republican district.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. John Spiros, R-Marshfield, faces Democrat John Small. Spiros is expected to win the heavily Republican district.
Assembly.primary-results: In a battle of incumbents, Spiros defeated Rozar by a double-digit margin and will face Small who was uncontested.

Assembly.district-info: The northwestern district covers parts of Marathon, Waupaca, Shawano and Portage counties, as well as the cities of Mosinee, Marion and Schofield. It includes villages like Big Falls, Birnamwood and Eland. It's a safe Republican district.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Pat Snyder, R-Schofield, announced he is moving to the 85th District despite being drawn into the 87th District under new redistricting maps. Mosinee Mayor Brent Jacobson faces Shawano County Board member William Switalla, a Democrat from Wittenberg. Jacobson, an attorney and small business owner, is focusing on fiscal responsibility in the district. Switalla is the village president of Wittenberg and has served on the Shawano County Board. He calls himself a moderate Democrat. Jacobson is favored to win due to the partisan composition of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: Jacobson soundly won the Republican primary and will face Switalla who was uncontested.

Assembly.district-info: This district covers the southeastern part of Green Bay, including Allouez and Bellevue, and stretches down toward De Pere. It is a toss-up district.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: First-time candidates Republican Ben Franklin and Democrat Christy Welch, both of De Pere, face off in the Nov. 5 election. Franklin is an Air Force veteran and small business owner. Welch, who serves as chair of the Democratic Party of Brown County, is centering her campaign around Medicaid and childcare expansion, increased public education funding and reproductive rights. The district is one to watch as Democrats try to win an Assembly majority.
Assembly.primary-results: Franklin soundly won the Republican primary and will face Welch who was uncontested.

Assembly.district-info: This southwestern Green Bay district includes Ashwaubenon and borders the Fox River to the east. It is a toss-up district.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell:
Two candidates with law enforcement experience will vie for a toss-up seat in the Nov. 5 election. The seat is one to watch as Republicans defend their Assembly majority.

Patrick Buckley of Green Bay, a Republican and chair of the Brown County Board, is a former Green Bay police officer and business owner. He lost a mayoral campaign to current Green Bay Mayor Eric Genrich in 2019.

Ryan Spaude of Green Bay, a Democrat, serves as a prosecutor in the Brown County District Attorney's office.
Assembly.primary-results: Both Buckley and Spaude advanced without an opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The 90th Assembly District covers central Green Bay. It is a likely Democratic seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Kristina Shelton, D-Green Bay, chose not to seek reelection. Democrat Amaad Rivera-Wagner, the Green Bay mayor's chief of staff, is running against Republican Jessica Henderson. Rivera-Wagner serves as the co-chair of the Greater Green Bay Chamber's Diversity and Inclusion Task Force and is targeting mental health, working families and safer streets as his campaign's platform. Henderson has a social media page, but it includes no information about her campaign. Rivera-Wagner is favored to win due to the partisan composition of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: Both Rivera-Wagner and Henderson advanced without an opponent.

Assembly.district-info: This district includes parts of Eau Claire, the city of Altoona, and the villages of Augusta, Fall Creek, Fairchild and Cadott. It is a Democratic -eaning seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell:
Rep. Jodi Emerson, D-Eau Claire, faces a challenge from Republican Eau Claire County Board Supervisor Michele Skinner. Emerson is favored due to the partisan composition of the district.

Emerson, first elected in 2018, emphasizes the need for affordable housing, tax cuts for small businesses, targeted medical care and access to IVF treatment. Emerson authored a package of housing bills to increase workforce and senior housing throughout the state.

Skinner serves on the Lake Altoona Rehabilitation and Protection District board and plans to tackle clean water, affordable housing and the environment. She also worked at TV stations for many years, and now believes her neutral perspectives can accommodate both sides of political aisle.
Assembly.primary-results: Both Emerson and Emerson advanced without an opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The district encompasses Menomonie and Chippewa Falls and lies to the north of Eau Claire. It is a toss-up district.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Incumbent Rep. Clint Moses, R-Menomonie, faces former Rep. Joseph Plouff, D-Menomonie. First elected in 2020, Moses chairs the Assembly Committee on Health, Aging and Long-Term Care. He also serves on the Assembly Agriculture Committee. Plouff served in the Assembly between 1997 and 2005. He's running again to curb gun violence, protect the environment and "make Wisconsin work for the people." The race is one to watch as Republicans defend their Assembly majority.
Assembly.primary-results: Plouff eked out a win in the Democratic primary and will face Moses in the general election.

Assembly.district-info: The district covers parts of Eau Claire, Trempealeau and Dunn counties. It includes the western half of the city of Eau Claire, along with the city of Osseo and the villages of Eleva and Strum. It also contains the University of Wisconsin–Eau Claire campus. It is a likely Democratic district.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Warren Petryk, R-Town of Washington, decided to retire after serving in the Assembly for over a decade. Christian Phelps of Eau Claire faces James Rolbiecki of Eau Claire. Phelps is a local nonprofit organizer, journalist and education advocate. Rolbiecki works in real estate, but grew up working at his family’s small business. He says he wants to use his entrepreneurial skills to improve the district. Phelps is favored to win after redistricting changed the partisan composition of the district.
Assembly.primary-results: Phelps narrowly won the Democratic primary and will face Rolbiecki in the general election.

Assembly.district-info: This district covers parts of La Crosse and Trempealeau counties. It includes the cities of Galesville and Onalaska, and the villages of Ettrick, Holmen and West Salem, along with part of the north side of La Crosse. It is a toss-up district.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell:
Incumbent Rep. Steve Doyle, D-Onalaska, faces a rematch against Republican Ryan Huebsch, of Onalaska, in the Nov. 5 election. Huebsch lost to Doyle by only 756 votes in 2022. Doyle has represented the 94th District since 2011. He has served on several bipartisan legislative task forces, including one on suicide prevention.

Huebsch is endorsed by the La Crosse County sheriff, Wisconsin Right to Life, the NRA and multiple state senators and representatives. His father, Mike Huebsch, previously represented the 94th District for 16 years, served as Assembly speaker and served in Gov. Scott Walker's cabinet.

The district is one to watch as Democrats try to win an Assembly majority.
Assembly.primary-results: Both Doyle and Huebsch advanced without an opponent  setting up a rematch of the 2022 contest.

Assembly.district-info: Assembly District 95 includes the northern half of La Crosse and stretches eastward to cover Sparta and Norwalk. It is a likely Democratic seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell:
Incumbent Rep. Jill Billings, D-La Crosse, faces a challenge from Republican Cedric Schnitzler in the Nov. 5 election. Billings is favored to win due to the partisan composition of the district.

Billings served on the La Crosse County Board for eight years before assuming legislative office in 2011. She has focused on supporting paid family medical leave, Medicaid expansion and environmental protection in La Crosse. She supported Gov. Tony Evers' funding increases for K-12 public schools and child care.

Schnitzler is a lifelong Monroe County resident, raised by his mom, a factory worker, and his dad, a roofer. He has served on the county board for 30 years and is now the Monroe County Board chair. He emphasizes tax cuts for working families, environmental protection and rural broadband expansion.
Assembly.primary-results: Both Billings and Schnitzler advanced without an opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The 96th Assembly District includes the southern half of La Crosse and all of Vernon County. It is a likely Democratic seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Incumbent Rep. Loren Oldenburg, R-Viroqua, faces Tara Johnson of La Crosse. Last year, Oldenburg and other Republicans sponsored an "Iowa-style" redistricting bill, which would have allowed the nonpartisan Legislative Reference Bureau to draw the new maps. Johnson is the former La Crosse County Board chair. Johnson is favored after redistricting shifted the district to be more heavily Democratic.
Assembly.primary-results: Johnson soundly won the Democratic primary and will face Oldenberg who was uncontested.

Assembly.district-info: This district stretches across Waukesha and Jefferson counties and includes the towns of Delafield, Eagle, Genesee, Ottawa and parts of Mukwonago. It is a safe Republican seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell:
Rep. Cindi Duchow, R-Delafield, squares off against Democrat Beth Leonard in the Nov. 5 election. Duchow is favored to win due to the partisan composition of the district.

Duchow, who has represented the 99th Assembly District since 2015 but was moved into the 97th District after redistricting, is now seeking re-election to cut taxes for retirees and provide government accountability. She serves on the Committee on Criminal Justice and Public Safety, as well as the Committees on Education, Financial Institutions and Insurance.

Leonard does not have any website with listed policy and goals for her campaign.
Assembly.primary-results: Both Duchow and Leonard advanced without an opponent.

Assembly.district-info: The 98th Assembly District covers several municipalities north of Waukesha, including Hartford and Sussex. It is a safe Republican seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Jim Piwowarczyk, of Hubertus, a former law enforcement officer and a co-founder of conservative news site Wisconsin Right Now, faces Democrat Del Schmechel. Piwowarczyk is campaigning on eliminating the state's income tax and improving public safety. The district heavily favors the Republican candidate.
Assembly.primary-results: Piwowarczyk won the Republican primary by a comfortable margin and will face Schmechel who was uncontested.

Assembly.district-info: The 99th Assembly District covers Oconomowoc and the northeastern corner of Waukesha County, and it extends northward to include parts of Jefferson and Dodge counties. It is a safe Republican seat.
Assembly.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Barb Dittrich, R-Oconomowoc, does not have a general election opponent. She was first elected in 2018 in a different district, but moved into the 99th after the recent redistricting. Dittrich supports private school vouchers, wants restrictions on transgender students playing on women's sports teams and authored “Kayleigh’s Law" which received bipartisan support and offers victims the chance to be granted lifetime restraining orders against their assailants.
Assembly.primary-results: Dittrich won the Republican primary by a comfortable margin and does not face a general election opponent.

Senate.district-race-nutshell: This seat is not up for election until 2026.

Senate.district-info: This safe Republican district covers a largely rural area west of Green Bay, including parts of Oconto, Menominee, Shawano, Outagamie and Brown counties.
Senate.district-race-nutshell:
Sen. Robert Cowles, R-Green Bay, plans to retire rather than seek reelection, ending what is currently the longest incumbent term in the Wisconsin Legislature.

Sen. Eric Wimberger, R-Green Bay, is running for the seat after redistricting moved him from the 30th Senate District, which he currently represents, to the more rural 2nd Senate District. In statements on his campaign website, Wimberger said he would support regulatory reforms relating to "eliminating burdensome red tape" and that he wanted to lower tax costs for businesses. Wimberger also said that he would focus on improving road conditions in northeast Wisconsin, support PFAS cleanup and to "stop SEL and DEI in Schools," acronyms that refer to Social and Emotional Learning and Diversity, Equity and Inclusion.

Kelly Peterson, a De Pere resident and former broadcast journalist with CBS 5 in Green Bay, is running as a Democrat. In her April campaign announcement, Peterson spoke out against Republican efforts to restrict abortion. Peterson is also campaigning on issues of child care affordability, farming and PFAS contamination.
This seat is not up for election until 2026.

Senate.district-info: This safe Democratic district includes portions of Milwaukee, Shorewood and Glendale, stretching west to the border of Milwaukee and Waukesha counties.
Senate.district-race-nutshell:
Sen. Lena Taylor, who was appointed to the Milwaukee County Circuit Court by Gov. Tony Evers, stepped down from the seat earlier this year.

Rep. Dora Drake won a July 2 special election to become the district's senator and the Democratic primary, both times against Rep. LaKeshia Myers.

Drake, who was elected to the Assembly in 2020, wants to bring the “next generation” of public servants to the Senate, she said. The 31-year-old is campaigning on her ability to work across the aisle and pass legislation, noting in an interview that she’s worked on more than 20 bills that have become law despite serving in the minority. 

She does not face a general election opponent.
This seat is not up for election until 2026.
