Senate.district-info: This safe Democratic district is contained within Milwaukee County, including parts of downtown Milwaukee, Wauwatosa and the Marquette University campus. It is one of two majority-Black Senate districts in Wisconsin.
Senate.district-race-nutshell: Incumbent Sen. LaTonya Johnson, D-Milwaukee, is running uncontested in the district, which she has represented since 2017. She is a member of the Legislature's powerful budget-writing committee.
This seat is not up for election until 2026.

Senate.district-info: This Republican-leaning district includes parts of Milwaukee, Ozaukee, Washington and Waukesha counties. It includes the cities of Cedarburg, Port Washington and Mequon, as well as villages like Bayside, Menomonee Falls and Whitefish Bay.
Senate.district-race-nutshell: New legislative maps drew incumbents Duey Stroebel, R-Saukville, and Dan Knodl, R-Germantown, into the same district. Knodl, rather than face Stroebel in a primary, decided to run for the Assembly instead. Stroebel, who has held office since 2015, will be challenged by Milwaukee Democrat Jodi Habush Sinykin. Sinykin lost to Knodl by only 1,200 votes in a special election for the district last year. She is a lawyer, business owner and environmental advocate. In March, Stroebel blocked the formation of a task force on missing and murdered African American women and girls. He has been a proponent of tax cuts and giving lawmakers oversight of executive branch rulemaking while serving in the Legislature. The district is one to watch as Democrats try to reduce the Republican Senate supermajority.
This seat is not up for election until 2026.

Senate.district-info: This likely Republican district includes all of Buffalo, Pepin, Pierce and St. Croix counties, and parts of Trempealeau and Dunn counties. It contains cities like Hudson, Arcadia and River Falls, as well as small villages like Ellsworth.
Senate.district-race-nutshell: Incumbent Sen. Rob Stafsholt, R-New Richmond, faces a challenge from Paul Hambleton, a Democrat from Hudson. Stafsholt was first elected to the Senate in 2020 after serving four years in the Assembly. Stafsholt authored a bill passed in February that cuts real estate property taxes and allows more funding to go to local governments. His Wisconsin and Minnesota income tax reciprocity bill was also signed into law by Gov. Tony Evers, as well as three bills he authored aimed at streamlining workforce licensing. Hambleton is a former teacher and public education advocate. He is focused on public education, affordability issues and expanding access to rural health care.
This seat is not up for election until 2026.

Senate.district-info: This safe Republican district contains Florence, Forest, Langlade, Lincoln, Marinette, Oneida, and Vilas counties, as well as parts of Oconto, Shawano and Marathon counties. It includes the cities of Antigo, Eagle River, Marinette, Rhinelander and Tomahawk.
Senate.district-race-nutshell: Incumbent Sen. Mary Felzkowski, R-Tomahawk, has represented the district since 2021. She will be challenged by Andi Rich, a Democrat from Marinette. Felzkowski recently sponsored a 14-week abortion ban that failed, as well as as bill that would have required local approval for the development of certain wind and solar projects. Gov. Tony Evers recently signed two of her bills into law that improve access to dental care in rural areas. Rich has a background in insurance and business and says she understands the importance of responsible taxpayer spending. She wants to tackle environmental issues like PFAS contamination, and she is focused on public school funding.
This seat is not up for election until 2026.

Senate.district-info: This Democratic-leaning district stretches from the Madison area north and west to encompass Portage, Wisconsin Dells, Baraboo, Reedsburg and Richland Center.
Senate.district-race-nutshell:
State Sen. Joan Ballweg, R-Markesan, is moving into this Democratic-leaning district to run for a second term in the state Senate. Ballweg, who serves as majority caucus vice chair, was drawn into the 13th Senate District under the state's new voting maps, pairing her with Sen. John Jagler, R-Watertown. To avoid an incumbent-on-incumbent matchup in two years, she opted to move into the new 14th Senate District. 

Ballweg chairs the Senate Committee on Agriculture and Tourism. During the most recent legislative session, she broke with her Republican colleagues and voted against legislation that would have banned transgender girls from playing on girls sports teams at public and voucher schools.

Democratic candidate Sarah Keyeski, of Lodi, is a mental health counselor who grew up on a dairy farm. She's campaigning on boosting public school funding and lifting revenue limits, bolstering access to abortion care, IVF and birth control and investing in broadband expansion in rural parts of the state.

The district is one to watch as Democrats try to reduce the Republican Senate supermajority.
This seat is not up for election until 2026.

Senate.district-info: This safe Democratic seat in the Madison area encompasses Fitchburg, Stoughton, Cottage Grove and Sun Prairie.
Senate.district-race-nutshell: Rep. Melissa Ratcliff of Cottage Grove, who has a trans son, said she will highlight her advocacy for the LGBTQ community and the work she did this session “to push back against the hateful anti-trans bills that come forward” while talking to voters. She won a three-way Democratic primary against two other state representatives. She does not face a general election opponent.
This seat is not up for election until 2026.

Senate.district-info: Bordering the northwestern edge of Lake Winnebago, this Fox Valley district covers urban centers across Appleton, Neenah and Oshkosh. It is a Democratic-leaning seat.
Senate.district-race-nutshell:
Democrat Kristi Alfheim, currently an Appleton Common Council alderperson, is pursuing a Senate seat for the second time after losing to Rachael Cabral-Guevara, R-Appleton, in the 19th Senate District in 2022. Now redistricted into the 18th Senate District, Alfheim is campaigning on women's rights, education and health care, according to an interview.

Republican Anthony Phillips, an Appleton resident and cancer physician, indicated in a statement on his campaign website that he is against abortion, supports "cutting taxes and red tape" for businesses and wants to spend on road and transportation infrastructure.

The district is one to watch as Democrats try to reduce the Republican Senate supermajority.
This seat is not up for election until 2026.

Senate.district-info: The district covers Fond du Lac and stretches into rural parts of Fond du Lac, Dodge, Washington, Sheboygan and Ozaukee counties. It is a safe Republican seat.
Senate.district-race-nutshell:
Incumbent Sen. Dan Feyen, R-Fond du Lac, is seeking a third term. Feyen has represented the 20th Senate District since 2016 and has been at the forefront of many Republican legislative efforts in the Senate as assistant majority leader.

Democrat Michael Rapp of Van Dyne said in a statement on his campaign website that he would support closing tax loopholes for the wealthy and large corporations, give public schools more resources and expand BadgerCare.
This seat is not up for election until 2026.

Senate.district-info: This likely Democratic seat stretches along Lake Michigan from Pleasant Prairie in Kenosha County to Sturtevant in Racine County.
Senate.district-race-nutshell: Incumbent Sen. Robert Wirch, D-Pleasant Prairie, is running uncontested in the district, which he has represented since 1997.
This seat is not up for election until 2026.

Senate.district-info: This Republican-leaning district stretches from Stevens Point to Juneau to Jackson.
Senate.district-race-nutshell:
Incumbent Sen. Patrick Testin, R-Stevens Point, was first elected to the state Senate in 2016. He currently serves as president pro tempore of the chamber and chairs the Senate Committee on Labor, Regulatory Reform, Veterans and Military Affairs. He's also a member of the Legislature's powerful budget-writing committee. Testin finished second in the 2022 Republican primary for lieutenant governor.

Challenger Collin McNamara, a Democrat from Stevens Point, graduated from the University of Wisconsin-Stevens Point in 2022 and is campaigning on improving health care access in central Wisconsin, investing in public schools and bolstering the middle class.
This seat is not up for election until 2026.

Senate.district-info: This safe Democratic seat encompasses downtown Madison, the city's lakes and Monona.
Senate.district-race-nutshell: Incumbent Sen. Kelda Roys, D-Madison, is running uncontested in the district, which she has represented since 2021. She is a member of the Legislature's powerful budget-writing committee.
This seat is not up for election until 2026.

Senate.district-info: This safe Republican district encompasses Muskego and Mukwonago.
Senate.district-race-nutshell:
Sen. Julian Bradley, R-Franklin, is moving into this safe Republican seat after being drawn into a district with fellow GOP Sen. Van Wanggaard, R-Racine. Bradley chaired the Legislative Council Study Committee on the Regulation of Artificial Intelligence in Wisconsin during the most recent legislative session and also served on the powerful Joint Committee for Review of Administrative Rules.

Democrat Megan Lach, a digital marketer from Waukesha, is "determined to be a voice for change and to advocate for stability, integrity, and service in state government."
This seat is not up for election until 2026.

Senate.district-info: This competitive district covers the metropolitan Green Bay region and is a toss-up seat.
Senate.district-race-nutshell:
Allouez Village President Jim Rafter is running as a Republican after serving on the Allouez Village Board for nearly a decade. Rafter, who has been a vocal advocate for the closure of Green Bay Correctional Institute, said in an interview that he hopes to reduce abortions, appropriate more state funding to local communities, increase more school funding and reduce political polarization in government.

Jamie Wall, a business consultant from Green Bay, is running as a Democrat. Wall, who previously lost two campaigns to represent Congress in 2006 and 2012, said in an interview that he intended to represent the "moderate majority of Wisconsin." Wall said that his priorities include expanding BadgerCare, supporting PFAS cleanup while holding polluters accountable and allocating more state funding to local communities.

The district is one to watch as Democrats try to reduce the Republican Senate supermajority.
This seat is not up for election until 2026.

Senate.district-info: This likely Democratic seat in western Wisconsin is anchored in La Crosse and includes portions of Vernon and Monroe counties.
Senate.district-race-nutshell:
Sen. Brad Pfaff, D-Onalaska, is seeking a second term in the state Senate in this likely Democratic seat in western Wisconsin. Pfaff serves on the Senate Committee on Agriculture and Tourism and previously served as acting secretary of the Wisconsin Department of Agriculture, Trade and Consumer Protection. The state Senate rejected his appointment in November 2019, effectively firing him from the job.

Republican Stacey Klein, a Trempealeau County Board member, is campaigning on cutting taxes, securing "parental rights" in the educational setting and bolstering mental health care in western Wisconsin.

The district is one to watch as Democrats try to reduce the Republican Senate supermajority.
This seat is not up for election until 2026.

US Congress.district-race-nutshell:
Incumbent U.S. Rep. Bryan Steil, R-Janesville, faces no GOP challenger in the Aug. 13 primary. First elected in 2018, Steil chairs the House Administration Committee. As of June 30, he had almost $4.7 million in his campaign account.

Democrat Peter Barca, from Kenosha, a former state lawmaker, member of the U.S. House and secretary of the state Department of Revenue, is challenging Steil. After four terms in the Assembly, Barca represented the 1st Congressional District in the U.S. House from 1993 to 1995, winning the seat in a special election. He narrowly lost his reelection bid. From 2009 to 2019 he returned to serving in the state Assembly including six years as minority leader. He served as revenue secretary from 2019 until earlier this year. Barca finished the most recent fundraising period with $630,000 in the bank.

Chester Todd, of Racine, is also on the ballot as the Green Party's nominee. He's running "to lead the charge toward social justice, environmental protection, peace at home and abroad, and an environment where grassroots democracy is the norm," according to his campaign website. No fundraising figures were available for Todd.
US Congress.primary-results: Steil and Barca both advanced. Neither faced a primary opponent.

US Congress.district-info: This Republican-leaning district stretches from Janesville along the Illinois border to include Kenosha, Racine and parts of southern Milwaukee County.
US Congress.district-race-nutshell: Incumbent U.S. Rep. Mark Pocan, D-Black Earth, is seeking a seventh term in office in November. A former co-chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, Pocan is a vocal critic of the United States' massive defense budget. He's also been critical of the U.S. response to the war in Gaza. Pocan faces Erik Olsen, a Madison native and attorney. Pocan is heavily favored to win re-election due to the partisan makeup of the district.
US Congress.primary-results: Olsen won the Republican primary and faces Pocan who didn't have a primary opponent.

US Congress.district-info: This Republican-leaning district encompasses 18 counties. It spans most of western Wisconsin and includes a mixture of small Democratic-leaning cities — La Crosse, Eau Claire and Stevens Point — and rural Republican communities near the Minnesota border.
US Congress.district-race-nutshell:
Freshman U.S. Rep. Derrick Van Orden has been a vocal critic of President Joe Biden and an ally of former President Donald Trump, Van Orden first won his seat in 2022 after longtime Democratic Rep. Ron Kind retired. 

Van Orden has the resources to mount a competitive reelection campaign, though he has attracted negative headlines for his conduct in Washington. For example, he drew bipartisan rebukes after reports surfaced that he yelled and cursed at a group of high-school-aged Senate pages. He has sought to appeal to more moderate voters over the past year. For example, after a train derailment in his district last summer, Van Orden introduced legislation that would bolster the National Transportation Safety Board’s investigative abilities.

He faces small-business owner Rebecca Cooke, who says Van Orden has failed the residents of his district and his constituents deserve a representative who can get things done.

Van Orden’s seat is seen by both national and Wisconsin Democrats as a prime flip opportunity to help them win back the U.S. House in November.
US Congress.primary-results: Cooke won a close Democratic primary and faces Van Orden who didn't have a primary opponent.

US Congress.district-info: This safe Democratic seat encompasses the city of Milwaukee.
US Congress.district-race-nutshell:
Longtime U.S. Rep. Gwen Moore, D-Milwaukee, is running for an 11th term in November. The state lawmaker turned congresswoman has represented the district since 2005 and is a heavyweight in Wisconsin Democratic politics. She is a member of the Congressional Progressive Caucus.

She faces Republican Tim Rogers, a Milwaukee native. He says he's in the race to bring clean drinking water to the city of Milwaukee. "I am running for political office not to complain about the situation, but to get involved and make the changes needed," he says on his campaign website.

Independent candidate Robert Raymond, an attorney, is also on the ballot.
US Congress.primary-results: Moore and Rogers both advanced. Moore did not face a primary opponent.

US Congress.district-info: This safe Republican district encompasses Waukesha, Jefferson and Washington counties. It also includes portions of Dodge County.
US Congress.district-race-nutshell:
Incumbent U.S. Rep. Scott Fitzgerald, R-Juneau, is seeking a third term in the U.S. House. Fitzgerald served in the state Senate for 16 years before being elected to Congress, including eight as majority leader. Fitzgerald was among the more than 100 GOP members of the U.S. House to object to counting Arizona's and Pennsylvania's electoral votes in the 2020 presidential election – one of his first acts in office. He serves on the House Judiciary Committee.

Fitzgerald faces a challenge from Democrat Ben Steinhoff, a paramedic. He's campaigning on building a health care system that "covers every American," bolstering abortion rights and legalizing marijuana. Fitzgerald is heavily favored to win re-election due to the partisan composition of the district.
US Congress.primary-results: Fitzgerald and Steinhoff both advanced. Neither faced a primary opponent.

US Congress.district-info: This likely Republican district includes Ozaukee, Sheboygan and Manitowoc counties along Lake Michigan. It stretches west to include Columbia, Marquette and Waushara counties, as well as Fond du Lac and Winnebago counties.
US Congress.district-race-nutshell:
U.S. Rep. Glenn Grothman, R-Glenbeulah, is seeking a sixth term in the U.S. House, breaking a 2014 pledge to only serve five terms in Congress. First elected in 2014, Grothman defeated longtime Rep. Tom Petri in a primary by running to his right. He currently serves on the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee.

Democrat John Zarbano, a retired attorney from Oshkosh, will challenge Grothman in November. He's campaigning on bolstering abortion rights, updating the U.S. immigration system and strengthening Social Security and Medicare.

Grothman is favored to win due to the partisan composition of the district.
US Congress.primary-results: Grothman and Zarbano both advanced. Neither faced a primary opponent.

US Congress.district-info: This safe Republican district covers most of northern and northwestern Wisconsin.
US Congress.district-race-nutshell:
Incumbent U.S. Rep. Tom Tiffany, R-Hazelhurst, is seeking a third full term in the U.S. House. First elected to Congress in a May 2020 special election, Tiffany previously spent a decade serving in the state Legislature. In December 2020, Tiffany was one of 126 GOP House members to sign onto an amicus brief submitted in support of a U.S. Supreme Court case contesting the results of the 2020 presidential election.

Tiffany faces Democrat Kyle Kilbourn, of Harshaw, who is campaigning on creating "a health care system where everyone can get the care they need, when they need it, without having to worry about a bill."

Tiffany is favored to win re-election due to the partisan composition of the district.
US Congress.primary-results: Kilbourn defeated Duanceau by a double-digit margin and faces Tiffany who didn't have a primary opponent.

US Congress.district-info: This likely Republican district is anchored in Green Bay and encompasses most of northeastern Wisconsin.
US Congress.district-race-nutshell:
U.S. Rep. Mike Gallagher, a Republican, resigned from the seat in April. The district leans Republican and featured a hotly contested Republican primary.

Republican Tony Wied, a businessman from De Pere who used to own a series of dinosaur-themed gas stations, has earned the endorsement of former President Donald Trump. He's campaigning on securing the southern border, curbing government spending and getting government "out of the way to unleash American energy resources."

Democrat Kristin Lyerly, an OB/GYN from De Pere, is campaigning on lowering prescription drug prices and bolstering abortion rights.
US Congress.primary-results: Wied, the candidate endorsed by Donald Trump, won a three-way primary against two candidates with legislative experience. He faces Lyerly who did not have a primary opponent.

Governor.district-info: This Republican-leaning district stretches from Janesville along the Illinois border to include Kenosha, Racine and parts of southern Milwaukee County.
Governor.district-race-nutshell:
Democratic Gov. Tony Evers is retiring after eight years. 

Several Democrats are vying for the nomination.

The most prominent Republican running is U.S. Rep. Tom Tiffany.

Lieutenant Gov.district-info: This Republican-leaning district stretches from Janesville along the Illinois border to include Kenosha, Racine and parts of southern Milwaukee County.
Lieutenant Gov.district-race-nutshell:
Incumbent U.S. Rep. Bryan Steil, R-Janesville, faces no GOP challenger in the Aug. 13 primary. First elected in 2018, Steil chairs the House Administration Committee. As of June 30, he had almost $4.7 million in his campaign account.
